free_tier.stated: No free tier. The smallest NAT container is USD 3.50 a year, one term of 12 months, and the page prints the same USD 3.50 as the renewal.

retention.stated: The container persists while the annual term is paid. The order page states 'No Refunds' as a checkbox the buyer must accept, and gives no suspension or deletion schedule.

egress.terms: 125 GB a month on the 128MB plan. More is bought in 125 GB blocks at USD 1.00 each; the page states no throttle after the allowance, only a price.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 8.00 per TB (125 GB blocks at USD 1.00)

interface_detail: Root shell inside an OpenVZ container; the order page offers Linux templates from AlmaLinux 8/9 and CentOS 7 to Debian 11/12 and Ubuntu 20.04/22.04.
tooling: Any SSH client. OpenVZ means no custom kernel and no kernel module of your own, which matters for WireGuard: it works only if the host kernel already carries the module.
chaining: A 128 MB always-on box on a shared IPv4 with 20 forwarded ports, for a WireGuard endpoint or an uptime probe that must cost nothing.

limits.value: 125 GB a month of transfer on the 128MB plan
one shared NAT IPv4; the order page warns some of its IPs are blocked by China, Russia and Iran

binding_note: 125 GB a month is the first hard number reached; 128 MB of RAM limits what runs but does not fail on a schedule.

notes: It renews at the same rate. There is no refund at all: the order form carries a mandatory 'I understand that there are no refunds' checkbox. The operator names no company and is one person, contacted at support@gullo.me and a +1 781 number; the community calls the owner 'Cam'. It is the only vendor in the sub-dollar band with a first-hand public report of WireGuard running on it: a LowEndTalk user installed precompiled wireguard-go and ran it with shadowsocks 'without running out of ram' over 255 days of uptime, and another confirms TUN/TAP can be enabled. That is a report that somebody did it, not a measurement that it works today. UDP on the 20 forwarded ports is still unstated by the vendor. | 2026-10-24: the UDP question is still open. Five pages were read today - the packages page, the pricing table, the NAT IPv4 help page, the knowledge-base index and the WireGuard how-to - and none of them says whether the 20 forwarded ports carry UDP. What the vendor does say is that WireGuard should be installed with wireguard-go, which is the userspace implementation an OpenVZ guest needs when the host kernel has no module. The pricing table also puts the 256 MB rung at USD 6.50-10.00 a year (USD 0.54-0.83 a month), so a beefier Gullo box is available inside the band if UDP turns out to be fine.
